cls: Recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) - hematopoietic growth factor / myeloid stimulant (biologic)
pharm: A non-glycosylated recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor produced in E. coli that binds GM-CSF receptors on myeloid progenitors, stimulating proliferation, differentiation, and functional activation of neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, and other myeloid cells to raise white-cell counts and enhance host defense.
quick: About 5-10 micrograms/kg/day SC (or IV infusion); max ~10 mcg/kg/day
Not applicable - given by subcutaneous injection or IV infusion
Avoid unless clearly necessary; human safety data lacking
Monitor; cautious use in renal impairment
Monitor liver function; caution in hepatic impairment
CBC/WBC and differential, platelets, fluid status, liver/renal function
summary: Molgramostim is a non-glycosylated recombinant human GM-CSF (E. coli-derived) marketed in Europe (e.g., Leucomax) chiefly to shorten neutropenia and reduce infection risk after myelosuppressive chemotherapy or bone-marrow transplantation, and to manage drug-induced (e.g., ganciclovir-related) neutropenia; it is not FDA-approved. As a biologic, authoritative dosing/safety information must be drawn from the EMA/SmPC and product insert (the data here reflect those sources and product literature). It is given by subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion, typically about 5-10 micrograms/kg/day, and stimulates production and activation of neutrophils and monocytes/macrophages. Characteristic effects include bone pain, fever/chills, and injection-site reactions; a first-dose reaction (dyspnea/hypotension) and, at higher doses, capillary-leak syndrome with edema and effusions can occur. It is contraindicated with hypersensitivity to GM-CSF or yeast/E. coli-derived product components and should not be given concurrently with (or within ~24 hours of) cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy. A newer inhaled molgramostim product is under development/approval for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis; the dosing here refers to the systemic neutropenia setting.
indications: Reduction of the duration of neutropenia and associated infection risk following myelosuppressive cytotoxic chemotherapy
Acceleration of myeloid (neutrophil) recovery after autologous or allogeneic bone-marrow transplantation
Management of drug-induced neutropenia (e.g., ganciclovir-induced neutropenia)

dosage.n: Begin after, not concurrent with, the chemotherapy cycle; continue per neutrophil recovery

dosage.t: IV infusion over 4-6 hours daily, starting the day of transplant; continued ~1 month
dosage.n: Titrate to neutrophil recovery per protocol/insert

dosage.d: Do not give within ~24 hours before or after chemotherapy/radiotherapy
dosage.n: Concurrent administration with cytotoxic therapy is contraindicated

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion as specified by the indication/insert
Reconstitute and prepare per the product insert; inspect the solution before use
Do not administer concurrently with, or within about 24 hours of, cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy
Rotate subcutaneous injection sites to reduce local reactions
Have monitoring/supportive measures available for a possible first-dose reaction (dyspnea, hypotension)
Store refrigerated and protect per insert; do not shake vigorously (protein product)
moa: Molgramostim is recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), a hematopoietic growth factor. It binds to GM-CSF receptors on the surface of myeloid progenitor cells and mature effector cells, activating intracellular signaling (JAK/STAT and related pathways) that drives proliferation and differentiation of granulocyte (neutrophil), monocyte/macrophage, and other myeloid lineages. It also enhances the function of mature cells - phagocytosis, oxidative burst, antibody-dependent cytotoxicity, and antigen presentation - thereby increasing circulating neutrophil and monocyte counts and bolstering host defense against infection. This shortens the depth and duration of chemotherapy- or transplant-related neutropenia.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to GM-CSF, molgramostim, or to yeast/E. coli-derived product components or excipients
Concomitant administration with cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy (and within ~24 hours before/after)
Excessive (>=10%) myeloid blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood (myeloid malignancy stimulation risk)
relative: Pre-existing fluid overload, pleural/pericardial effusion, or capillary-leak risk
Significant cardiac, renal, or hepatic impairment
monitor: Complete blood count with differential and platelets (avoid excessive leukocytosis)
Fluid status / weight, blood pressure, and signs of capillary-leak syndrome or effusions
Injection-site and systemic (fever, bone pain) reactions

preg: There are no adequate human safety data; use during pregnancy should be avoided unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk to the fetus. As a recombinant protein, formal reproductive risk data are limited - reflecting EMA/insert-based information.
lact: It is not known whether molgramostim is excreted in human milk. Because of the lack of data and the potential for adverse effects in the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: Specific renal dose adjustments are not well defined; monitor renal function and use with caution in patients with renal impairment, particularly given the potential for fluid shifts and capillary-leak syndrome.
hepatic: Transient elevations of liver enzymes have been reported with GM-CSF therapy. Monitor liver function and use with caution in hepatic impairment; specific dose adjustments are not well established.

major: Cytotoxic chemotherapy / radiotherapy - must not be given concurrently or within ~24 hours, as rapidly dividing myeloid cells are more sensitive to cytotoxic damage and efficacy is compromised
moderate: Corticosteroids - may potentiate myeloproliferative/inflammatory effects and leukocytosis
Lithium - may potentiate the leukocyte-stimulating effect
Other myeloid growth factors - additive effects on white-cell counts
minor: No significant cytochrome P450 metabolic interactions (a protein, cleared by catabolism/receptor-mediated uptake)
interactions.diagnostics: Causes leukocytosis and may transiently elevate alkaline phosphatase, LDH, and liver enzymes; can affect bone-scan and other lab interpretations - interpret counts in clinical context.

serious: First-dose reaction (dyspnea and hypotension within hours of the first dose)
rare: Worsening of underlying inflammatory or autoimmune disease
emergency: Severe first-dose reaction with respiratory distress and hypotension

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelet count, frequently, to guide dosing and avoid excessive leukocytosis
Body weight, fluid balance, blood pressure, and signs of capillary-leak syndrome or effusions
Close observation around the first dose for dyspnea/hypotension
Temperature and infection status; injection-site reactions
Pulmonary/cardiac status if dyspnea, edema, or chest symptoms develop
counsel: This medicine is a protein given by injection under the skin or into a vein, usually in hospital or clinic
Bone pain, muscle aches, fever, and chills are common and can often be eased with simple analgesics - tell your team if severe
Report shortness of breath, swelling, rapid weight gain, or dizziness, especially after the first dose
Tell your team about any allergy to this drug, to GM-CSF, or to yeast/E. coli-based products
It is not given on the same day as your chemotherapy or radiotherapy
Keep all blood-test appointments so your white-cell count can be checked
Store as instructed (usually refrigerated) and do not shake the vial
pk: Neutrophil/monocyte counts begin to rise within days of starting therapy
Plasma peaks within a few hours of subcutaneous dosing
Short - on the order of 1-2 hours (somewhat longer than glycosylated GM-CSF)
White-cell counts fall toward baseline within days of stopping; dosed daily
Store refrigerated (2-8 C) per insert; protect from light and do not shake or freeze
pearls: BIOLOGIC and NOT FDA-approved - authoritative dosing/safety must come from the EMA/SmPC and product insert (e.g., Leucomax); data here are insert/literature-based
Non-glycosylated E. coli-derived rhuGM-CSF; stimulates neutrophils AND monocytes/macrophages (broader than G-CSF)
Do NOT give within ~24 hours of cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy
Watch for the first-dose reaction (dyspnea/hypotension) and, at higher doses, capillary-leak syndrome
More inflammatory toxicity (fever, bone pain) than G-CSF - it was withdrawn from some markets in favor of G-CSF
Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to GM-CSF or yeast/E. coli-derived components
A separate inhaled molgramostim product is being developed/approved for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (different dosing)
missed: Doses are given by a healthcare professional on a set schedule. If a scheduled dose is missed, contact the treating team for advice on timing of the next dose - do not give two doses close together to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose may produce marked leukocytosis and amplified adverse effects (fever, bone pain, dyspnea/hypotension, capillary-leak syndrome). Stop the drug and provide supportive care with hemodynamic and respiratory support, fluid management for capillary leak, and monitoring of blood counts until they normalize.
